spans.text: Ange pushes open the door and leaves the boisterous place behind.
Now that she knows the busy and lively scene was all a sham, she finds it rather sickening.
The gold coin weighs heavily in her pocket, signifying that everything that just happened was real.
...Now, she must hurry back to her apartment and discuss how to proceed with Task Force DEFY.
Frau Ange.
While Ange is still deep in thought, someone calls her name softly from next to her.
Almost out of reflex, Ange pulls back and executes a kick.
Smack!
The kick produces such a loud noise Ange thinks she kicked a sandbag.
But the brief exchange is all it takes for her to take in her interceptor.
One second, please.
Tsk.
Since her first kick didn't do the job, Ange delivers a second one without even a pause.
Whoa!
The man seems to have expected Ange's attack and nimbly sidesteps it, causing her kick to miss a second time.
But Ange isn't fazed either.
Boom!
Her alloy fist smashes into the brick wall. If this punch had landed on a person, they would've been hospitalized for months.
Backed up against the wall with the small crater a mere inch away from his ear, the young man looks a little unnerved.
But Ange could see that he didn't make the slightest attempt to dodge her punch just now.
He knew⁠—with absolute certainty—that Ange would not hit him, so he did not even flinch.
Who are you?
The man rubs the arm he used to block Ange's first kick and looks at her apologetically.
I saw that kick coming, but it was more powerful than I'd anticipated. You really are formidable.
He speaks in a perfectly even tone—neither humble nor haughty. Despite being at Ange's mercy, he shows no sign of panic.
Answer my question. Or the next punch will smash your brains out.
You are not one to murder innocent people, Frau Angelia.
I can make an exception today.
And you are anything but innocent, not to mention rude.
Pardon me... I haven't even introduced myself.
As you can see, I am a Stasi agent.
Ange's brow furrows.
Only then does she notice that this man doesn't look older than 20.
What does the Stasi want with me now?
Don't tell me you want to send me back to lock me up for a few more days?
No, that's not it.
In fact...
Light blinks, the very image of innocence.
I'm here to help you.
Welcome back.
Ange, are you alright?!
Ange catches sight of her two familiar subordinates the moment she enters the temporary ops room.
She frowns as she shifts her gaze from the Dolls to the man sitting in front of the monitors.
You've brought my subordinates here. What's the big idea, J?
Hey, don't give me that murderous look, eh?
It took a lot of work to pull these DEFY ladies out from among the rioting mob and gather them all, you know?
We found this place ourselves.
Did you have to expose me straight away?!
Thanks for the work, J.
The young man follows Ange into the room and greets J politely before turning to address the DEFY Dolls.
As per our agreement, I have delivered Frau Angelia safely to you.
Well done. If you'd taken another minute, our leader would've clawed her way out through the roof.
12, explain.
There's nothing much to explain.
When we got separated from you in the crowd, we immediately realized it would be extremely difficult to regroup.
So we changed strategies and decided to track down those who were monitoring us instead.
That's how you found this place?
It didn't take much effort. After all, they still knew exactly where we were under those circumstances.
It was either GPS trackers or having a high vantage point.
Once we understood that, it wasn't difficult figuring out the rest.
When we got here, we found out that Mr. J was the one in charge of this operation.
He told us that you were safe and had us wait here while he sent someone to fetch you.
12 refused to cooperate at first and threw a tantrum.
It was kinda noisy, but then we got used to it.
It wasn't that noisy.
I don't trust them. J did a decent job in Bremen,
But ensuring Ange's safety is my top priority.
I only agreed to wait because I believe in Ange.
So...have you had your meeting?
How did it go?
I got some information and possible leads.
At the very least, I now have some idea about what to do.
So you're the aid that he promised?
Ange eyes Light and J, her gaze moving back and forth between them until finally settling on J.
Are you in any shape to help? Your injuries look pretty bad.
What, wanna spar, wardmate? I don't know who you're talking about, but we are indeed under official order to aid you.
It took us some time, but we eventually managed to take over this operation. Now Light and I are in charge of keeping tabs on you.
In other words, you can move around freely in Berlin.
So who exactly was he, Ange?
...The "Earl ".
Ange fishes out the gold coin from her pocket and rubs the intricate markings with her thumb.
A glistening griffin is etched onto the coin.
Or should I say...
Griffin Lyons.
Y-You mean...THAT Griffin?
THE Griffin in "Griffin and Kryuger"?
I hear he...
Yeah, if I'm not mistaken, it's him in the flesh.
I don't work for him, but he is very close with Zelinsky and Old Misha...
I can't tell if he can be trusted, but at the very least, he is on our side.
So... Uh, nevermind. I didn't hear anything.
What happens next is none of my business.
Light, I'm leaving you in charge of everything.
Me?
You, duh. K sent me—a poor injured man—here, while he himself stayed behind in Bremen, having the time of his life.
Not that he expected I would have to work in the field.
In any case, I leave this in your capable hands.
You haven't asked for my opinion.
Well, any objections?
He doesn't look old enough to drink.
He may be young, but he's the most exceptional up-and-coming agent in the Stasi. You've seen what he's capable of, haven't you?
He's been commanding the operation to monitor you single-handedly. I didn't do anything.
So he's been wasting his "exceptional" talent on spying on us?
If I were you, I'd have already started investigating William's movements in Berlin.
If you hadn't been wasting precious time, I would've tracked down Leone and the others by now.
I looked into it, Frau Angelia.
...What?
I don't know what your current objective is.
But before I came to Berlin, I took over the investigation you were conducting in Bremen and followed through with the remaining leads.
I have recorded everything in detail and compiled profiles...
...concerning the culprits arrested in Bremen—Leone, Hopps, and Powell.
He's telling the truth, Ange. I read them.
You read them?
I couldn't very well just sit here and wait, could I?
The three of them have been transported to Berlin for imprisonment.
But you're not gonna believe this.
Leone was released due to mental illness. She's now living quite a cushy life at a sanatorium.
Still in Berlin, obviously.
According to my investigation, everything about Leone's release was highly dubious.
I suspect a person of authority pulled some strings to protect her, but I have no others clues for the time being.
...Explain the situation to me in detail.
Yes, ma'am.
Wait, hold on.
You're not planning to have this conversation here, are you?
This really isn't the greatest spot, so I suggest you guys take this somewhere else... After all, you're free to go anywhere now.
I agree, Ange.
Surely you have a lot to discuss with us...
About your conversation with Grif...the Earl ?
...Alright, let's go back to the apartment then.
I'll come with you.
And I'll pass.
The protagonist shall retreat behind the scenes for now. Young people should be given the time to shine every now and then.
Isn't that right, Light? Now that you're back in your hometown, don't forget to make time to visit your—
Let's go, Frau Angelia.
Sure.
Ange glances at the youth with delicate features.
He's young, brave, remarkable, and ambitious... Just like her when she was young.
But just for a brief second...
His face overlaps with Morridow's in her mind.
